The '''1985–86 Bundesliga''' was the 23rd season of the [[Bundesliga]], the premier football league in [[West Germany]]. It began on 9 August 1985<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=326204 |title=Schedule Round 1 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608085220/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=326204 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> and ended on 26 April 1986.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=326287 |title=Archive 1985/1986 Round 34 |publisher=DFB |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608085233/https://www.dfb.de/index.php?id=326287 |archive-date=8 June 2011 }}</ref> [[Bayern Munich]] were the defending champions.

==Competition modus==
Every team played two games against each other team, one at home and one away. Teams received two points for a win and one point for a draw. If two or more teams were tied on points, places were determined by [[goal difference]] and, if still tied, by goals scored. The team with the most points were crowned champions while the two teams with the fewest points were relegated to [[2. Bundesliga]]. The third-to-last team had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off against the third-placed team from 2. Bundesliga.

==Team changes to 1984–85==
[[Karlsruher SC]] and [[Eintracht Braunschweig]] were directly relegated to the [[1985–86 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] after finishing in the last two places. They were replaced by [[1. FC Nürnberg]] and [[Hannover 96]]. Karlsruhe and Braunschweig were eventually joined in demotion by relegation/promotion play-off participant [[Arminia Bielefeld]], who lost on aggregate against [[1. FC Saarbrücken]].

==Relegation play-offs==
[[Borussia Dortmund]] and third-placed [[1985–86 2. Bundesliga|2. Bundesliga]] team [[SC Fortuna Köln]] had to compete in a two-legged relegation/promotion play-off. After a two-leg series, both teams were tied 3–3 on aggregate, so a deciding third match had to be scheduled. Dortmund won this match, 8–0, and retained their Bundesliga status.
